title: Product law of correlated sign pairs
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $[0m\rho\in[-1,1]$. Draw $n$ independent sign pairs, each with first sign uniform on $[0m\{-1,1\}$ and with the second sign obtained by retaining the first with probability $(1+ho)/2$ and flipping it otherwise. Regard the pairs as two sign vectors using the coordinatewise pairing. Their joint distribution equals the law formed by choosing the first vector uniformly and then independently applying this same sign noise to each coordinate to obtain the second vector.
